Independent VFX Research Reference
Designing readable and expressive effects from reusable parts
For future Roblox games and an independently authored VFX designer reference. Research reviewed through 13 October 2026.
Great effects make an action understandable and felt. Start with what happened, where, when and how consequential it is. Then use shape, value, colour, timing and composition to concentrate attention. Reusable flipbooks, particles, beams, trails, parts, lights and post effects can support this job when their layers have distinct purposes.
This is an independent research input for a later comparison with a separately researched Claude report. It is not the final cross-model synthesis and does not implement the future agent.
Use it to select and tune existing assets, diagnose weak effects and define project-specific tests. Engine limits are not artistic defaults. Published examples are not universal timing prescriptions. Every recipe and genre profile is explicitly an inference; unsupported quantities remain “no number found.”

How to use this reference

Start with Output 8 to specify the communication job. Consult Outputs 1 and 2 for component choices and a moment recipe. Use Outputs 3, 7 and 9 to preserve scene clarity, current engine behavior and review gates. Resolve evidence through the source IDs in the register. The companion package preserves the exact requested table headers in CSV and JSON; the document expands wide rows into readable labeled records.


Evidence and numerical discipline

Tiers: A is first-hand maker writing/talks, peer-reviewed research or clearly labeled preprints; Spec is Roblox Creator Docs; B is strong trade reporting with named makers; C is named expert teaching/community evidence. Tier D is not used as proof.
Evidence levels: study, preprint, industry practice, spec and inference. These are claim labels, not a single confidence score. A source may support a capability or observation without validating a proposed recipe.
Recency: modern sources are preferred. Retained pre-2020 classics are marked and linked to a newer qualification or an explicit follow-up gap. Catalog pages support metadata and stated scope only.
Numbers retain units, sample, timebase and task context. Inferred arithmetic is labeled. Missing values are “no number found” or null in the card template, never fabricated defaults. Tier C-only precision carries an explicit corroboration limit.
Every artist-derived feeling is a design hypothesis unless measured. No unconditional player-over-enemy hierarchy, universal layer count or fixed mobile particle budget was established. The most important actionable cue may be an edge rather than the brightest center.
Quotations were avoided; field terms and source titles are retained. The later synthesis should reconcile disagreements at the claim level and preserve contrary/null findings.

01 Element table

The practitioner headings organize controllable visual choices. Feeling and energy descriptions express design intent unless a study directly measured them. No universal safe count, duration, brightness ratio or emotional mapping is implied.

gameplay


Communication job

effect on feeling: Legibility supports confidence; wrong meaning creates frustration.
effect on energy: Match importance, not decoration.
numbers or ranges: no number found
mechanism: Communicate identity, consequence and magnitude; consistency lets players learn.
evidence level: industry practice; feeling inference
source, tier and year: ES-S03 (Tier C, 2020); ES-S02 (Tier A, 2021)

Importance rating

effect on feeling: Reserves awe for consequential events.
effect on energy: Relative escalation.
numbers or ranges: 1–10 per caster/enemy/ally in Beardilocks’s reported League exercise; exact scale singly sourced. No numerical mapping to render parameters found.
mechanism: Rank damage, control, dodgeability and decision relevance.
evidence level: industry practice; scale singly sourced
source, tier and year: ES-S03 (Tier C, 2020); ES-S02 (Tier A, 2021)

Truthful indicator

effect on feeling: Fairness and trust.
effect on energy: Urgency follows actual hazard.
numbers or ranges: no number found
mechanism: Primary border/time cue must represent the actionable area and state, regardless of ornamental halo.
evidence level: industry practice
source, tier and year: ES-S01 (Tier A, 2022); ES-S05 (Tier A, 2017) pre-2020

Shared status vocabulary

effect on feeling: Familiarity; quicker interpretation.
effect on energy: Depends on status.
numbers or ranges: no number found
mechanism: League-specific conventions: green/soft heal, vertical knockup, floor ring/cylinder root. A stun is not automatically a knockup.
evidence level: industry practice
source, tier and year: ES-S03 (Tier C, 2020); ES-S02 (Tier A, 2021)

Viewer specific visibility

effect on feeling: Less irrelevant spectacle.
effect on energy: Preserves attention for local decisions.
numbers or ranges: no number found
mechanism: Show information to people who can act on it; preserve enemy-facing identity.
evidence level: industry practice
source, tier and year: ES-S03 (Tier C, 2020); ES-S16 (Tier A, 2023)

Predicted versus confirmed hit

effect on feeling: Responsiveness without false success.
effect on energy: Immediate action, later confirmation.
numbers or ranges: VALORANT example: ≥1 rendered frame to muzzle/tracer; 40 ms one-way→80 ms round-trip plus processing.
mechanism: Client feedback and authoritative outcome can occur at different times. Distinguish their meanings.
evidence level: industry practice; Roblox transfer inference
source, tier and year: ES-S18 (Tier A, 2020)

shape


Curves and circles

effect on feeling: Softness/safety is a plausible starting hypothesis.
effect on energy: Usually calmer when motion is also smooth.
numbers or ranges: no number found
mechanism: Smooth contour scenes received safer judgements; a circle’s exact gameplay meaning remains learned.
evidence level: study; effect-design inference
source, tier and year: ES-S19 (Tier A, 2021)

Triangles spikes and jagged contours

effect on feeling: Potential threat, sharpness.
effect on energy: Can support aggressive emphasis.
numbers or ranges: no number found
mechanism: Contour combinations affect threat judgments; no universal triangle-to-danger mapping proved.
evidence level: study; effect-design inference
source, tier and year: ES-S19 (Tier A, 2021)

Squares and rigid geometry

effect on feeling: Stable, constructed or mechanical by convention.
effect on energy: Controlled or abrupt, depending on timing.
numbers or ranges: no number found
mechanism: Inference: select rectilinear assets for the game’s established mechanical vocabulary; test interpretation.
evidence level: inference

Swirls and spirals

effect on feeling: Magic, gathering or vortex by convention.
effect on energy: Rising with contraction/acceleration.
numbers or ranges: no number found
mechanism: Inference: inward flow can forecast a center; outward flow can show release. A decorative spiral is not a validated emotion trigger.
evidence level: inference

Hard and soft edges

effect on feeling: Crisp action with softer aftermath.
effect on energy: Sharp transitions can read as forceful.
numbers or ranges: no number found
mechanism: Distinct silhouette supports identification; soft secondary material should not replace the hit boundary.
evidence level: industry practice; arrangement inference
source, tier and year: ES-S05 (Tier A, 2017) pre-2020; ES-S07 (Tier A, 2023)

Silhouette and primary shape

effect on feeling: Immediate recognizability.
effect on energy: A clear shape can feel strong without more particles.
numbers or ranges: no number found
mechanism: Choose a flipbook whose silhouette survives scale reduction and does not resemble another action.
evidence level: industry practice; kitbash inference
source, tier and year: ES-S02 (Tier A, 2021); ES-S05 (Tier A, 2017) pre-2020

Line of action and directional blur

effect on feeling: Intent and speed.
effect on energy: Directional emphasis.
numbers or ranges: no number found; inspect a paused frame.
mechanism: A projectile tail should indicate travel direction; orient trails and stretched parts along the actual path.
evidence level: industry practice; kitbash inference
source, tier and year: ES-S02 (Tier A, 2021)

Arcs and radial versus directional release

effect on feeling: Flow versus centered blast.
effect on energy: Spread conveys release; aimed motion conveys intent.
numbers or ranges: no number found
mechanism: Arcs support secondary movement. Pick radial sheets for outward events, streaks/beams for directed events.
evidence level: industry practice; asset-selection inference
source, tier and year: ES-S09 (Tier A, 2018) pre-2020; ES-S07 (Tier A, 2023)

Texture detail breakup and erosion

effect on feeling: Organic richness; excessive detail can read as noise.
effect on energy: Fine random change may add apparent agitation.
numbers or ranges: no number found
mechanism: Reduce superfluous fine texture before increasing brightness; select coarser variants for small projections.
evidence level: industry practice; mobile transfer inference
source, tier and year: ES-S01 (Tier A, 2022)

Scale squash and stretch

effect on feeling: Weight, flexibility or punch, depending on sequence.
effect on energy: Temporal scale contrast.
numbers or ranges: no number found for a general character-size ratio.
mechanism: Inference: tune visual scale separately from collision size; use squash/stretch for art without falsifying borders.
evidence level: inference informed by industry practice
source, tier and year: ES-S09 (Tier A, 2018) pre-2020

value


Focal light dark contrast

effect on feeling: Clear emphasis.
effect on energy: Strong local contrast can elevate a peak.
numbers or ranges: no number found
mechanism: Contrast is relational: inspect the effect against the actual background and competitors.
evidence level: industry practice
source, tier and year: ES-S04 (Tier C, 2020); ES-S17 (Tier A, 2020)

Mid range bias and reserved extremes

effect on feeling: Room for special peaks and UI.
effect on energy: Keeps ordinary actions below peaks.
numbers or ranges: 0% and 100% discouraged in LoL; no numeric middle-band limits found.
mechanism: A title-specific allocation of value, not a physical law. Sparkball uses bolder values where restraint failed.
evidence level: industry practice; contextual disagreement
source, tier and year: ES-S05 (Tier A, 2017) pre-2020; ES-S07 (Tier A, 2023)

Bright core and dimmer support

effect on feeling: Magic or concentrated force.
effect on energy: Focused intensity.
numbers or ranges: no number found
mechanism: Make the important region distinct; broad uniform white removes internal structure.
evidence level: industry practice; failure analysis inference
source, tier and year: ES-S06 (Tier C, 2022); ES-S04 (Tier C, 2020)

Glow emissive appearance and bloom

effect on feeling: Radiance, heat or magic.
effect on energy: Can increase apparent intensity.
numbers or ranges: no number found
mechanism: Inference: asset glow affects the image; actual world lights and post bloom are separate layers with separate costs. Check readability without optional polish.
evidence level: inference

World illumination

effect on feeling: Connection to surrounding space.
effect on energy: A coordinated light pulse can reinforce a peak.
numbers or ranges: no number found
mechanism: Inference: place a brief world-light response at the same spatial event; avoid large uniform wash that erases silhouettes.
evidence level: inference

colour


Dominant hue plus accent

effect on feeling: Coherence rather than competing signals.
effect on energy: Accent supplies controlled emphasis.
numbers or ranges: One dominant hue role; no percentage split found.
mechanism: Complementary hues need hierarchy; palette width is a design choice.
evidence level: industry practice
source, tier and year: ES-S05 (Tier A, 2017) pre-2020; ES-S06 (Tier C, 2022)

Saturation relative to stage

effect on feeling: Noticeability rather than guaranteed excitement.
effect on energy: Relative boost only.
numbers or ranges: no number found for a universal saturation range.
mechanism: High saturation is useful only relative to context; brightest/most saturated does not guarantee gaze.
evidence level: industry practice + study; inference
source, tier and year: ES-S07 (Tier A, 2023); ES-S13 (Tier A, 2021)

Core edge separation

effect on feeling: Concentrated energy with readable perimeter.
effect on energy: Peak at core or actionable edge as needed.
numbers or ranges: no number found
mechanism: Inference: recolour layers by function; do not insist every effect has a white center when the border is the gameplay message.
evidence level: inference

Colour over life

effect on feeling: Cooling, exhaustion, decay.
effect on energy: Descending energy.
numbers or ranges: no number found
mechanism: Inference: hot-core→warm flame→dark smoke is a material/story cue, not a universal recipe; choose library states and tint curves accordingly.
evidence level: inference

Hue meaning team and danger colours

effect on feeling: Learned meaning; cultural associations vary.
effect on energy: No fixed hue-to-energy law.
numbers or ranges: 4598 participants; 30 nations; 22 languages; r=.88 association-pattern similarity.
mechanism: Study measured colour terms and emotion associations, not emotions induced by VFX. Keep team identity consistent and redundant with shape.
evidence level: study; game-language inference
source, tier and year: ES-S20 (Tier A, 2020)

timing


Windup anticipation

effect on feeling: Expectation, warning, gathering power.
effect on energy: Rising toward action.
numbers or ranges: no number found for general windup milliseconds.
mechanism: Communicate impending gameplay when a reaction window exists; cosmetic windup must not delay responsive controls.
evidence level: industry practice; implementation inference
source, tier and year: ES-S09 (Tier A, 2018) pre-2020; ES-S12 (Tier C, 2025)

Punch impact

effect on feeling: Impact, surprise, release.
effect on energy: Rapid peak.
numbers or ranges: no number found for general punch frames.
mechanism: A strong state change contrasts with preparation; align the visible consequence with the authored gameplay event.
evidence level: industry practice; implementation inference
source, tier and year: ES-S09 (Tier A, 2018) pre-2020; ES-S12 (Tier C, 2025)

Crescendo

effect on feeling: Anticipation, escalation, triumph.
effect on energy: Progressively stronger culmination.
numbers or ranges: no number found
mechanism: Coordinate changes in shape, motion, value and sound rather than raising every parameter equally.
evidence level: inference; practitioner terminology
source, tier and year: ES-S11 (Tier C, 2025)

Follow through overlapping action

effect on feeling: Residual force, believable settling.
effect on energy: Falls from peak; can preserve local activity.
numbers or ranges: no number found
mechanism: Different parts settle at different times; secondary action supports the main event.
evidence level: industry practice
source, tier and year: ES-S09 (Tier A, 2018) pre-2020; ES-S11 (Tier C, 2025)

Dissipation falloff

effect on feeling: Completion and cleared space.
effect on energy: Lowering.
numbers or ranges: no number found
mechanism: Retire the active signal when gameplay ends; residual art can lose opacity/value/size without suggesting continued danger.
evidence level: industry practice; implementation inference
source, tier and year: ES-S01 (Tier A, 2022); ES-S12 (Tier C, 2025)

Nonlinear speed holds slow in out

effect on feeling: Weight and deliberate force.
effect on energy: Contrast, not constant speed.
numbers or ranges: no number found
mechanism: Retiming can change interpretation; use curves and holds to serve the event, not because every parameter must ease.
evidence level: industry practice
source, tier and year: ES-S07 (Tier A, 2023); ES-S10 (Tier C, 2025)

Sparkball snappy action heuristic

effect on feeling: Brief readable action with an outro.
effect on energy: Early concentration.
numbers or ranges: Main action finished or dissipating by first 25% of lifetime, reported for Sparkball.
mechanism: A named title-specific practice. Do not copy onto charges, sustained hazards or other games as a requirement.
evidence level: industry practice: firsthand Sparkball observation; no independent validation; not a universal default
source, tier and year: ES-S07 (Tier A, 2023)

Shape breakup versus opacity fade

effect on feeling: Designed erosion can feel less like a card vanishing.
effect on energy: Energy disperses.
numbers or ranges: no number found
mechanism: Inference: prefer a suitable premade breakup sequence when available; fade is not inherently wrong, and state expiry may need a crisp end.
evidence level: inference informed by industry practice
source, tier and year: ES-S07 (Tier A, 2023)

Linger smoke decals and scorch

effect on feeling: Aftermath, history, scale; possible obstruction.
effect on energy: Lower-intensity persistence.
numbers or ranges: no number found
mechanism: Inference: separate cosmetic residue from active-damage cues; preserve enemy, pickup and path visibility.
evidence level: inference

Frame exposure and stepped animation

effect on feeling: Graphic, hand-animated cadence.
effect on energy: Cadence is distinct from event duration.
numbers or ranges: Arithmetic: frame duration=1000/fps ms; on 2s at 24 fps=83.33 ms per drawing, not a universal 12 fps game setting.
mechanism: Inference: preserve cadence while timing the hit marker independently; display, simulation and flipbook rates are different.
evidence level: inference; arithmetic only

composition


Primary secondary and tertiary roles

effect on feeling: Purposeful richness.
effect on energy: One meaningful emphasis within the event.
numbers or ranges: no number found for optimal emitter/layer count.
mechanism: Roles are not a mandate for three emitters. Name what each component contributes before adding it.
evidence level: industry practice; kitbash inference
source, tier and year: ES-S04 (Tier C, 2020); ES-S08 (Tier C, undated)

Areas of focus and rest

effect on feeling: Ease of reading; a place for the eye to settle.
effect on energy: Contrast between active and quiet regions.
numbers or ranges: no number found
mechanism: The gameplay-bearing feature owns emphasis; decorative motion should not compete equally.
evidence level: industry practice
source, tier and year: ES-S04 (Tier C, 2020); ES-S02 (Tier A, 2021)

Particle density and clumping

effect on feeling: Sparse can feel delicate; dense can feel substantial or muddy.
effect on energy: Density is not equivalent to impact.
numbers or ranges: no number found for a universal particle cap.
mechanism: Inference: compare clustered and uniform emission at equal cost; inspect whether empty spaces preserve semantic boundaries.
evidence level: inference

Crowding and peripheral recognition

effect on feeling: Confusion when nearby elements become difficult to distinguish.
effect on energy: More activity may reduce usable information.
numbers or ranges: n=50; 82%/94% model variance explained, not a screen budget.
mechanism: Spacing and eccentricity affect identification; tests used letters, not combat particles.
evidence level: study; game transfer inference
source, tier and year: ES-S15 (Tier A, 2023)

Saliency and task relevance

effect on feeling: Attention can follow meaning instead of brightness.
effect on energy: High saliency need not mean high usefulness.
numbers or ranges: Model≈20 Hz selection; not an effect timing recommendation.
mechanism: Goals, history, reward, scene structure and bottom-up features jointly guide search.
evidence level: study (theoretical review)
source, tier and year: ES-S13 (Tier A, 2021)

Abrupt motion onset

effect on feeling: Alerting or distraction, conditional on task.
effect on energy: Sudden rise.
numbers or ranges: Study E1+59 ms RT, d=.41; E2+3 ms, p=.436, d=.026.
mechanism: An irrelevant rotation onset captured attention in one search mode and was avoided in another.
evidence level: study
source, tier and year: ES-S14 (Tier A, 2026)

Looming rapid expansion

effect on feeling: Approach or imminent-event hypothesis.
effect on energy: Can increase urgency.
numbers or ranges: ERP effects 140/280 ms; no usable VFX detection threshold found.
mechanism: Looming interacted with emotion/distance; reaction-time main effect was nonsignificant.
evidence level: study; effect-design inference
source, tier and year: ES-S21 (Tier A, 2022)

camera


Screen shake

effect on feeling: Intended force or instability; may be annoying.
effect on energy: Brief accent versus prolonged disturbance.
numbers or ranges: Eiserloh model: trauma t in [0,1]; shake proportional to t² or t³. No universal amplitude, frequency or duration found.
mechanism: Industry model: event accumulation and linear decay drive smoothed-noise motion. Use separate amplitude, frequency and recovery controls; comfort guidance favors optional reduction/off.
evidence level: industry practice; application inference
source, tier and year: CAM01 A 2016 pre-2020; SA04 A 2022 living guidance

Hit stop freeze

effect on feeling: Intended emphasis at contact.
effect on energy: Pause then release.
numbers or ranges: Lin reports Guilty Gear Xrd light hit-stop 7 frames and heavy approximately 10 frames; reference fps unverified, so no ms conversion. These are observations, not defaults.
mechanism: Lin reports title-specific examples, without validated frame-rate conversion. Inference: distinguish world, animation, camera and local-VFX pause; local visuals do not pause server damage.
evidence level: preprint observation; implementation inference
source, tier and year: JS03 A 2022 preprint

Camera kick

effect on feeling: Directional recoil/force.
effect on energy: Fast displacement then recovery.
numbers or ranges: no number found
mechanism: Inference: align kick direction to action, preserve control and test recovery while tracking another target.
evidence level: inference

Zoom FOV pulse

effect on feeling: Intended focus, speed or scale emphasis.
effect on energy: Change of visual extent.
numbers or ranges: no number found
mechanism: Lin describes cinematic camera focus/zoom examples. Inference: test projected hitbox readability throughout FOV changes; preserve a reduced-motion option.
evidence level: preprint (observational); design inference
source, tier and year: ES-S27 (Tier A, 2022)

Slow motion

effect on feeling: Inspection, drama, stretched consequence.
effect on energy: Temporal expansion.
numbers or ranges: no number found
mechanism: Lin describes finishing-attack slow-motion examples. Inference: separate spectacle timing from player reaction and multiplayer simulation; a local effect rate is not global slow motion.
evidence level: preprint (observational); design inference
source, tier and year: ES-S27 (Tier A, 2022)

Flash impact frame inversion

effect on feeling: Intended sharp emphasis or shock.
effect on energy: Abrupt contrast peak.
numbers or ranges: no number found for an aesthetic default; safety criteria are in Output 3.
mechanism: Inference: bind the flash to the actual moment; test the aggregate sequence, including overlapping effects, for safety.
evidence level: inference

Vignette

effect on feeling: Intended edge framing, injury or mood.
effect on energy: May lower peripheral information.
numbers or ranges: no number found
mechanism: Inference: never make the obscured periphery carry the only usable hazard cue.
evidence level: inference

Chromatic aberration

effect on feeling: Stylized distortion or disorientation.
effect on energy: Potentially agitated image.
numbers or ranges: no number found
mechanism: Inference: judge benefit against split-edge loss of precision; preserve a reduced-effects alternative.
evidence level: inference

Radial motion blur

effect on feeling: Intended speed or energetic focus.
effect on energy: Can concentrate apparent motion.
numbers or ranges: no number found
mechanism: Inference: distinguish a directional asset smear from full-screen blur; retain readable target and path detail.
evidence level: inference

Depth of field

effect on feeling: Cinematic focal isolation.
effect on energy: Quiet background or narrow attention.
numbers or ranges: no number found
mechanism: Inference: acceptable only while all required gameplay information stays legible; gameplay depth does not follow a film camera automatically.
evidence level: inference

02 Moment recipe table

All 54 recipes are proposed inferences assembled from the component principles. They are not measurements of the named films or games. Importance is relative to the player’s next decision; no unsupported numerical rating or phase duration is assigned.
Windup, punch, crescendo, follow-through and dissipation are available phases, not a requirement that every effect contain all five. Authoritative activation/contact/expiry wins over cosmetic timing. A rarity ladder is a proposed project convention, not evidence of an optimal reward or monetization design.

Hits


M01 Light hit

feeling: contact, responsiveness, satisfaction
importance rating: Below heavy hits and urgent threats; no number found for a prescribed score
communication job: A contact occurred here; show direction and ordinary damage
layers: Compact contact flipbook; directional flecks; brief target response
timing per phase (ms or frames): No number found. Windup follows the attack; punch at confirmed contact; follow-through exits along strike; dissipation clears before the next readable contact.
value and colour: Local high-value accent within the established damage palette
shape and motion: Small directional wedge or compressed ring; fast expansion then taper
camera and screen effect: Keep camera steady unless testing shows a clear benefit
sound sync point: Contact transient with contact image
what to leave out: Full-screen flash, smoke curtain, reward-like sparkle
examples from film, anime and games: League of Legends supplies hierarchy/indicator practice [ES-S01, ES-S02]; Lin’s Guilty Gear Xrd observations [JS03] concern hit-stop only. This particular build is an inferred transfer.
evidence level: inference: proposed kitbash recipe; component principles are evidenced separately, not a validated combination

M02 Heavy hit

feeling: weight, power, impact
importance rating: Above ordinary hits; below imminent lethal warning; no number found for a prescribed score
communication job: A stronger contact landed; retain target and follow-up attack visibility
layers: Dense contact core; broader directional breakup; grounded dust; sparse larger debris
timing per phase (ms or frames): No number found. Windup creates expectation; punch marks contact; follow-through transfers force into target and material; dissipation yields to the next decision.
value and colour: Bright compact core against lower-value mass; avoid raising every layer equally
shape and motion: Clear force axis; compressed core opens into larger uneven fragments
camera and screen effect: Optional local camera kick only under user settings; never treat shake as required
sound sync point: Contact transient at punch; separate body/debris tails
what to leave out: Long white wash, permanent shake, debris with uniform speed
examples from film, anime and games: League of Legends supplies hierarchy/indicator practice [ES-S01, ES-S02]; Lin’s Guilty Gear Xrd observations [JS03] concern hit-stop only. This particular build is an inferred transfer.
evidence level: inference: proposed kitbash recipe; component principles are evidenced separately, not a validated combination

M03 Critical hit

feeling: surprise, precision, heightened impact
importance rating: Above normal damage but retain threat hierarchy; no number found for a prescribed score
communication job: This hit met the game’s critical-hit condition
layers: Reuse base-hit identity; add distinctive shape or accent; critical UI cue
timing per phase (ms or frames): No number found. Punch at confirmed critical result; added accent follows the same event; cleanup avoids masking the next attack.
value and colour: Distinct accent plus redundant icon/shape; do not rely on hue alone
shape and motion: Sharper focal shape or stronger contrast, not all layers enlarged
camera and screen effect: Optional accent under reduced-motion/flash settings
sound sync point: Critical accent with confirmed damage
what to leave out: Changing the truthful contact point or hiding ordinary damage
examples from film, anime and games: League of Legends supplies hierarchy/indicator practice [ES-S01, ES-S02]; Lin’s Guilty Gear Xrd observations [JS03] concern hit-stop only. This particular build is an inferred transfer.
evidence level: inference: proposed kitbash recipe; component principles are evidenced separately, not a validated combination

M04 Final blow

feeling: completion, triumph, release
importance rating: High for participants; reduced for distant observers; no number found for a prescribed score
communication job: The target or encounter is definitively finished
layers: Terminal contact; readable defeat transition; restrained aftermath; objective confirmation
timing per phase (ms or frames): No number found. Punch at authoritative defeat; follow-through resolves the target; dissipation leaves the next objective readable.
value and colour: Peak contrast at completion then lower-value aftermath
shape and motion: Directional force resolves into a clean ending
camera and screen effect: Cinematic camera only when gameplay can safely yield control
sound sync point: Defeat transient at state change; aftermath tails afterwards
what to leave out: Celebration that hides a surviving threat; implying victory before confirmation
examples from film, anime and games: League of Legends supplies hierarchy/indicator practice [ES-S01, ES-S02]; Lin’s Guilty Gear Xrd observations [JS03] concern hit-stop only. This particular build is an inferred transfer.
evidence level: inference: proposed kitbash recipe; component principles are evidenced separately, not a validated combination

M05 Blocked hit

feeling: resistance, denial, firmness
importance rating: Equal to the information value of the block; no number found for a prescribed score
communication job: The attack contacted a defense and did not penetrate
layers: Shield/contact shape; redirected sparks; block-state cue
timing per phase (ms or frames): No number found. Punch at actual block; follow-through deflects away; dissipation quick enough to read another attempt.
value and colour: Distinct defense language; bright point at surface not inside defender
shape and motion: Hard stop and tangential reflection; preserve attack direction
camera and screen effect: Usually steady; defend-state cue should survive reduced motion
sound sync point: Block transient at surface contact
what to leave out: Using the same burst as successful damage; target-body explosion
examples from film, anime and games: League of Legends supplies hierarchy/indicator practice [ES-S01, ES-S02]; Lin’s Guilty Gear Xrd observations [JS03] concern hit-stop only. This particular build is an inferred transfer.
evidence level: inference: proposed kitbash recipe; component principles are evidenced separately, not a validated combination

Explosions


M06 Small explosion

feeling: snap, localized force
importance rating: Local event below nearby lethal threat; no number found for a prescribed score
communication job: Communicate source, actual hazard extent and the event’s state
layers: Compact hot core; brief directional fragments; small smoke residue
timing per phase (ms or frames): No number found. Windup exists only when gameplay grants warning; punch at detonation; follow-through carries fragments; dissipation reduces occlusion while residual hazards remain explicitly marked.
value and colour: Hot focal core and darker residue if appropriate to material; hazard boundary remains separate
shape and motion: Radial start constrained by source and surface
camera and screen effect: Camera response optional, distance-aware and reducible; no universal amplitude found
sound sync point: Detonation transient at visual impulse; secondary debris sounds follow contacts
what to leave out: Large shock ring suggesting a larger damage radius
examples from film, anime and games: Teardown, THE FINALS and Battlefield destruction methods in Output 4 [FM-S09, FM-S10, FM-S11, FM-S12, FM-S14, FM-S15] provide cause, material and debris examples. Material-specific kitbash and timings here remain inference.
evidence level: inference: proposed kitbash recipe; component principles are evidenced separately, not a validated combination

M07 Medium explosion

feeling: power, danger
importance rating: High for players within the actual threat; no number found for a prescribed score
communication job: Communicate source, actual hazard extent and the event’s state
layers: Core flipbook; pressure/dust skirt; selected debris; lower-value smoke
timing per phase (ms or frames): No number found. Windup exists only when gameplay grants warning; punch at detonation; follow-through carries fragments; dissipation reduces occlusion while residual hazards remain explicitly marked.
value and colour: Hot focal core and darker residue if appropriate to material; hazard boundary remains separate
shape and motion: Radial core with directional escape where geometry permits
camera and screen effect: Camera response optional, distance-aware and reducible; no universal amplitude found
sound sync point: Detonation transient at visual impulse; secondary debris sounds follow contacts
what to leave out: Uniform debris sphere or opaque screen-sized smoke

what to leave out: Dense fill hiding occupants; decorative rings mistaken for damaging area
examples from film, anime and games: League of Legends missile communication [ES-S03] and official clarity guidance [ES-S01, ES-S02] support source, path, state and threat readability; complete recipe is inference.
evidence level: inference: proposed kitbash recipe; component principles are evidenced separately, not a validated combination

Warnings and danger


M35 Truthful telegraph

feeling: anticipation, danger
importance rating: Highest when it enables avoiding harm; no number found for a prescribed score
communication job: Show exactly where and when the next hit will happen
layers: Boundary and timing cue; clear source/direction; redundant symbol
timing per phase (ms or frames): No number found. Timing is authoritative gameplay timing; no cosmetic lead or lag is prescribed. Maintain the cue for its real state and clear it when that state ends.
value and colour: Contrast against stage with redundant shape/text; test colour-vision variants
shape and motion: Boundary stays geometrically truthful; progress maps to the actual trigger
camera and screen effect: Avoid impairing control; preserve central visibility and reduced-flash mode
sound sync point: Actual warning/activation transitions
what to leave out: Bloom or flourishes extending the perceived area
examples from film, anime and games: League of Legends missile communication [ES-S03] and official clarity guidance [ES-S01, ES-S02] support source, path, state and threat readability; complete recipe is inference.
evidence level: inference: proposed kitbash recipe; component principles are evidenced separately, not a validated combination

Movement


M39 Dash

feeling: speed, decisive motion

communication job: Show source, destination and any damaging or invulnerable segment
layers: Short directional trail; source and arrival accents
timing per phase (ms or frames): No number found. Events synchronize with actual movement/contact; follow-through resolves at the destination; dissipation leaves the next navigation decision clear.
value and colour: Preserve character silhouette and path contrast; movement palette distinct from threat
shape and motion: Elongate along actual path; break trail across discontinuities
camera and screen effect: Do not force shake/zoom; keep navigation legible with reduced motion
sound sync point: Start and arrival events
what to leave out: Opaque body-length cloud hiding destination
examples from film, anime and games: Stylized film motion and cadence examples in Output 4 [FM-S18, FM-S19, FM-S20, FM-S23] are visual analogies only. They do not establish Roblox movement timing or camera defaults.
evidence level: inference: proposed kitbash recipe; component principles are evidenced separately, not a validated combination

UI effects


M50 Button press

03 Scene placement rulebook

Use these rules as observable checks. A number describes its stated source context only. When no transferable threshold exists, the pass/fail task replaces an invented screen percentage or particle cap.

V 01

Rule: Make the actionable edge match gameplay geometry.
Numbers: no number found
Pass or fail: Overlay collision/area debug view on the primary indicator at cast, impact and expiry; flag mismatches separately from decorative overflow.
Evidence: industry practice; test procedure inference; ES-S01, ES-S05

V 02

Rule: Assign importance separately for each viewer role.
Numbers: 1–10 is reported League practice; exact scale singly sourced.
Pass or fail: Record caster/enemy/ally priorities and the decision each visible cue supports.
Evidence: industry practice; workflow inference; ES-S03, ES-S16

V 03

Rule: Let the current actionable threat beat irrelevant spectacle.
Numbers: no number found
Pass or fail: Ask testers what they must react to while reward, ambient and ally effects run; record wrong-target reactions.
Evidence: industry practice; test procedure inference; ES-S02

V 04

Rule: Keep a recognisable primary shape across variants.
Numbers: no number found
Pass or fail: Blind-test ability identity for base/skin/recolour variants; reject a variant that changes the inferred action.
Evidence: industry practice; test procedure inference; ES-S02, ES-S16

V 05

Rule: Make projectile direction readable when paused.
Numbers: no number found
Pass or fail: Pause at several positions and ask travel direction; inspect head–tail ambiguity.
Evidence: industry practice; ES-S02

V 06

Rule: Remove irrelevant viewer-specific cues.
Numbers: no number found
Pass or fail: For each layer, document whose next action would change if it vanished; omit only genuinely noninformative variants.
Evidence: industry practice; test procedure inference; ES-S03, ES-S16

V 07

Rule: Reserve value and saturation headroom across the whole scene.
Numbers: no number found for universal brightness ratios or HSV bands.
Pass or fail: Inspect scene/character/VFX/UI simultaneously; identify unintended competitors at the moment of decision.
Evidence: industry practice; test procedure inference; ES-S05, ES-S07, ES-S17

V 08

Rule: Use the stage to support the effect.
Numbers: no number found
Pass or fail: Replay on brightest, darkest and most patterned permitted surfaces; adjust the background or effect contrast if recognition fails.
Evidence: industry practice; test procedure inference; ES-S02, ES-S17

V 09

Rule: Move ornament away from gameplay sightlines where possible.
Numbers: VALORANT reports most details above player height; no universal pixel-height rule.
Pass or fail: Check expected target/path screen regions under the actual camera; reduce decorative contrast in those regions.
Evidence: industry practice; top-down transfer inference; ES-S17

V 10

Rule: Budget overlap by decision performance, not emitter count alone.
Numbers: no number found for universal count, coverage or overdraw threshold.
Pass or fail: Run worst credible multiplayer overlaps on target phones; measure detection errors, response time, screen occlusion and GPU cost together.
Evidence: inference; ES-S15, ES-S26

V 11

Rule: Retire active hazard language when the hazard ends.
Numbers: no number found
Pass or fail: Stop on the final damage/status tick and inspect the remaining border/colour/motion; residue must not imply another hit.
Evidence: inference; ES-S01, ES-S12

V 12

Rule: Lower the prominence of aftermath.
Numbers: no number found
Pass or fail: Compare peak and residue under competing threats; flag residual smoke/light that attracts attention away from a new actionable cue.
Evidence: industry practice; test procedure inference; ES-S05, ES-S06

V 13

Rule: Check effects while the player is looking elsewhere.
Numbers: no number found
Pass or fail: Use a central tracking task plus peripheral warning; repeat at actual phone display size and camera distance.
Evidence: study-informed inference; ES-S13, ES-S15

V 14

Rule: Treat surprise onsets as a shared scene resource.
Numbers: no number found for a safe onset interval.
Pass or fail: Compare isolated and rapid overlapping bursts while targets move; record missed warnings and tracking loss.
Evidence: study-informed inference; ES-S22, ES-S14

V 15

Rule: Do not assume the brightest pixel wins.
Numbers: no number found
Pass or fail: Use eye tracking when available, otherwise timed recognition/choice tests; compare intended focus with observed choices.
Evidence: study-informed inference; ES-S13, ES-S14

V 16

Rule: Keep hit confirmation semantically distinct from firing.
Numbers: VALORANT example 80 ms plus processing from 40 ms one-way; not a Roblox budget.
Pass or fail: Test misses, predicted hits rejected by server, late confirmations and moving/crouching targets.
Evidence: industry practice; transfer inference; ES-S18

V 17

Rule: Check screen effects with player control active.
Numbers: no number found for universal shake amplitude, frequency or duration.
Pass or fail: Test aim, camera turn, jump/path navigation during kick/shake/zoom; retest with reduced effects.
Evidence: inference; 

V 18

Rule: Match the timing style to the gameplay contract.
Numbers: no number found
Pass or fail: Log cast/contact/peak/last-active/last-visible timestamps in milliseconds; do not add cosmetic delay to a required instant response.
Evidence: industry practice; test procedure inference; ES-S18, ES-S12

V 19

Rule: Build temporal contrast at scene level.
Numbers: no number found
Pass or fail: Compare ordinary play, buildup, payoff and aftermath; check that ordinary repeats have not consumed every available prominence cue.
Evidence: inference; ES-S26

V 20

Rule: Keep depth cues useful.
Numbers: no number found
Pass or fail: Review foreground particles, camera-near cards, fog and depth of field; confirm all required target/path cues remain available.
Evidence: inference; 

V 21

Rule: Test the composition with optional polish removed.
Numbers: no number found
Pass or fail: Disable bloom/world light/camera layers and inspect whether identity, hit extent and phase remain understandable.
Evidence: inference; ES-S10

V 22

Rule: Do not import film staging as a compulsory gameplay cut.
Numbers: no number found
Pass or fail: For a cinematic payoff, verify whether control and threats are intentionally paused; otherwise keep the gameplay view usable.
Evidence: inference; 

V 23

Rule: Calibrate screen measurements before interpreting them.
Numbers: duration_ms=1000×frames/fps; arithmetic conversion, not a tuning recommendation.
Pass or fail: Record viewport resolution, device, camera FOV/distance, capture frame rate and display frame rate beside every coverage or timing measurement.
Evidence: inference; 

V 24

Rule: Use a single problem statement for each review change.
Numbers: no number found
Pass or fail: Record moment, viewer, symptom, probable cause, exact parameter edit, protected gameplay meaning and a comparison test.
Evidence: industry practice; template inference; ES-S01, ES-S23

V 25

Rule: Check that observers can distinguish an attempted action, successful hit, blocked hit and completed outcome with the selected effect build.
Numbers: no universal threshold found
Pass or fail: Fail when a miss reads as success or a success cue is hidden by the preceding action.
Evidence: inference; JS01

V 26

Rule: Randomise only decorative dimensions whose variation cannot change the meaning or timing of a gameplay cue.
Numbers: No supported universal rotation, hue, size, timing-jitter range or variant count found.
Pass or fail: Hold collision boundary, contact cue, team identity and warning deadline invariant.
Evidence: inference; JS01, JS05

V 27

Rule: Stress-test the repeated event at the game’s actual maximum cadence and realistic multiplayer concurrency.
Numbers: Use the brief’s 1,000-event replay as an automated durability workload, not a clinically safe human exposure prescription.
Pass or fail: Fail if tails accumulate, UI stops being readable, the next contact is masked, or frame-time budget fails.
Evidence: inference; 

V 28

Rule: Keep cheap input confirmation available when decorative repetition is capped or suppressed.
Numbers: No universal cooldown, cap or ducking percentage found.
Pass or fail: Fail if an accepted action becomes indistinguishable from dropped input.
Evidence: inference; JS01

V 29

Rule: Tie combo escalation to a readable change in achieved outcome, then test bounded progression against constant feedback.
Numbers: No sourced step count, escalation increment, reset time or maximum intensity found.
Pass or fail: Fail if spectacle makes separate hits or the streak-reset state ambiguous; do not assume more streak juice raises retention.
Evidence: inference; JS01

V 30

Rule: Author one contact event that schedules the visual punch and sound transient together; measure actual output synchrony.
Numbers: No universal allowable game-impact delay found. Schedule from the same event, then measure displayed and audible output; no numerical offset default is prescribed.
Pass or fail: Check audio waveform onset against first visible contact/flash in captured output, including device latency and dropped frames.
Evidence: inference; AV01, JS05

V 31

Rule: Separate an intentional distant-explosion delay or anticipation sound from an accidental sync error.
Numbers: No universal sound-leading or picture-leading offset for hits found.
Pass or fail: The event card explicitly identifies the causal sync point and whether a nonzero offset is artistic/physical.
Evidence: inference; AV01, AV02

V 32

Rule: Assess the composite scene, including overlapping emitters, muzzle flashes, lighting, post effects, UI and camera movement.
Numbers: Evaluate every rolling 1-second interval; see SA01 criteria below.
Pass or fail: Per-asset passes are insufficient when the final combined output can exceed a criterion.
Evidence: inference; SA01, SA03

V 33

Rule: Do not use an accessibility toggle or seizure warning as the only response to known hazardous flashing.
Numbers: no number found
Pass or fail: Remove or redesign known failures before release; a player may encounter them before reaching settings.
Evidence: industry practice; SA02, SA03

V 34

Rule: Provide an off setting for nonessential camera shake, bob, motion blur and automatic camera movement.
Numbers: Halo Infinite example: separate 0–100% blur, shake, full-screen effect and speed-line controls. This scale specifies controls, not physical safe amplitude.
Pass or fail: Minimum setting fully removes the targeted nonessential motion; feedback remains interpretable.
Evidence: industry practice; SA04

V 35

Rule: Encode essential team, danger, rarity and state information with a non-colour signifier.
Numbers: At least one additional signifier: shape, pattern, icon or label.
Pass or fail: Correct interpretation remains possible without distinguishing the assigned hues; test with players, not simulation alone.
Evidence: industry practice; SA05

V 36

Rule: Use contrast ratios for important readable UI/markers, not as instructions to intensify every effect.
Numbers: XAG 102: standard important text/visual elements 4.5:1; large elements 3:1; high-contrast UI mode 7:1.
Pass or fail: Measure against the lowest-contrast local background; a glowing particle core does not certify the whole telegraph.
Evidence: industry practice; SA06

Safety and synchrony numbers with context


WCAG general flash definition

Value: Pair of opposing relative-luminance changes ≥0.10, with darker state <0.80. One brighten–darken pair is one flash.
Scope: sRGB relative luminance, not raw RGB differences or emitter Brightness
Evidence: SA01

WCAG SC 2 3 1 rate area routes

Value: No more than 3 general flashes and/or 3 red flashes in any 1-second period, OR combined concurrent flash area ≤0.006 sr within any 10° field (25% of that field) at typical viewing distance.
Scope: 25% is not a whole-screen allowance. SC 2.3.2 Level AAA removes the area alternative.
Evidence: SA01

WCAG saturated red working definition

Value: An opposing transition pair with one state R/(R+G+B)≥0.8 and state difference >0.2 in CIE 1976 UCS chromaticity.
Scope: Use a standards-aware analyzer; channels require defined colour-space handling.
Evidence: SA02

HDR other colour space flash assessment

Value: General flash: luminance change ≥20 cd/m² with darker state <160 cd/m²; when darker state ≥160 cd/m², Michelson contrast ≥1/17.
Scope: Test highest dynamic-range version. These values are not Roblox property settings.
Evidence: SA02

Microsoft XAG 118 criteria

Value: Approximate failure descriptions: >3 flashes/second and ≥20% screen; luminance change 10%, dark state <.8. Red formula (R−G−B)×320 change >20 with saturated-red ratio ≥.8.
Scope: Older red formula and approximate screen geometry differ from WCAG 2.2; also flags sustained lower-intensity flashing and high-contrast spatial patterns.
Evidence: SA03

Audiovisual laboratory result

Value: Li et al., Experiment 1, n=27 analyzed: action high-causality JND 143 ms vs low-causality 219 ms; d=1.86. High-causality action PSS −30 ms (their negative means audio leading).
Scope: Fitted simultaneity judgments on 30 fps, 3 s clips, offsets sampled every 200 ms. Not latency budgets for responsive game hits.
Evidence: AV01

Broadcast synchrony reference pre 2020

Value: ITU 1998 average detectability ~45 ms audio lead /125 ms audio lag; acceptability ~90 ms lead /185 ms lag.
Scope: Television material/assessment context. Detection is not acceptability; neither equals a recommended game-impact delay.
Evidence: AV02

Published hit stop observation

Value: Guilty Gear Xrd -SIGN-: 7 frames light, approximately 10 heavy; Dragon Ball FighterZ: approximately 1 s cinematic ultimate hold.
Scope: Descriptive examples, with no causal effect size or validated cross-game optimum; do not convert to milliseconds without verified game/capture frame rate.
Evidence: JS03

HardingFPA G2 capability

Value: HD SDR 1080p60; optional UHD SDR, live-feed or captured-gameplay analysis with frame/in-frame results.
Scope: Select correct guideline set. Listed SDR capability must not be assumed to validate HDR.
Evidence: SA07

04 Field methods table

Use documented production methods as references for staging and asset selection. A film frame can be tightly controlled; an interactive multiplayer scene cannot assume the same camera, timing or occlusion tolerance. Coverage gaps are retained rather than filled with famous titles or fan analysis.

how to use it in a game: Treat hitbox, direction and damage phase as constraints before recolor, glow, sparks or theme.
evidence level: Industry practice; game transfer is inference
source, tier and year: FM-S01 (A, 2022-04-25); FM-S02 (A, 2021-03-12)

Documented case studies


League of Legends

id: FM-C01
field: Real-time game readability
source ids: FM-S01; FM-S02
documented studio method: Truthful gameplay signaling is the first production priority; decorative theme follows.
transfer inference: Attach effect geometry to the actual attack footprint, then reserve stronger accents for more important events.
limits: No numerical readability thresholds established.
mechanism: Real-time gameplay VFX

VALORANT

id: FM-C02
field: Real-time game readability
source ids: FM-S03
documented studio method: Map art is deliberately simplified and tested around player visibility.
transfer inference: VFX review should include noisy and quiet backgrounds, not just a neutral showcase.
limits: Environment policy does not guarantee effect legibility on its own.
mechanism: Real-time scene design

Overwatch 2

id: FM-C03
field: Real-time game readability
source ids: FM-S04
documented studio method: Mythic skin presentation can differ by observer relationship.
transfer inference: Separate cosmetic ownership from enemy-critical recognition.
limits: Do not infer different hitboxes or damage indicators are acceptable.
mechanism: Real-time observer-specific cosmetic VFX

limits: A prefractured asset is not proof that every break is scripted; physical collapse and authoring are separate stages.

limits: Event schema proposed below is our synthesis, not copied engine architecture.
